newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium calls for urgent help for Zaire refugees.
newsitem.headline: Belgium calls for urgent help for Zaire refugees.

text.p: The European Union must take urgent action to help ease the misery of Hutu refugees being repatriated to Rwanda from Zaire, the Belgian government said in a letter to the Dutch Presidency of the bloc.

"The Belgian government is convinced of the urgent need for a European and/or international initiative to secure humanitarian aid," Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene and Foreign Minister Eric Derycke wrote.
The letter, extracts of which were published by the Belgian foreign ministry on Wednesday, was sent on Tuesday. Belgium is the former colonial power in what is now Zaire.

"The drama of last Sunday, when 91 refugees were trampled or suffocated to death on the train from Biaro to Kisangani, is the painful proof of the fact that the repatriation is being carried out in a disorganised manner," the letter said.

The government urged the EU to collaborate with U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees Sadako Ogata in sending observers to monitor whether rebel leader Laurent Kabila is keeping to his pledges on the peaceful repatriation of the refugees. It also offered logistic and financial help in organising such a move.
Kabila, whose forces are closing in on the Zairean capital Kinshasa, has drawn international condemnation over the plight of the Rwandan Hutu refugees.
